items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: The interviewee discusses the relationship between Louis Armstrong and Joel, stating 'the principle on which they were done were well-established between them' and describing how 'Oliver would signal... to Louis'. The interviewee (Al Rose) is narrating this interaction as a third party.

ctx.x: side of Louis, who, because of his unique musical capacities, could add greatly to the impact and artistic quality of any kind of a musical organization. But from a formal standpoint, there was no necessity for that. He was also following certain trends that had come into existence by that time of having larger augmented orchestras, and he felt the need of having some kind of a show on the stage, feeling that too small a group didn't look right.
Now, those coronet breaks that Louis and Joel did together, they were rehearsed, were they?

No, they weren't rehearsed, but I would say that the principle on which they were done were well-established between them. And the way it worked was that Oliver would signal the break that he was going to make to Louis by fingering the valves on his cornet, and Louis could immediately see what it was that he was going to do. And so when the break came, they would have these miraculous, and there's nothing short of that, two cornet breaks. Of course, jazz fans ever since have appreciated what took place on those…
